tdee-calculator.assumptionNote: TDEE is an estimate; real burn varies with tracking error, muscle mass and day-to-day life. Recalculate every few kilograms of change and adjust from real weight trends.
benefits: Ends guesswork: your maintenance calories come from your body and your life, not an average.
Goal targets turn lose/maintain/gain into one concrete daily number.
Shows exactly how much your activity level changes the equation.
The weekly pace estimate keeps expectations realistic.

faqs.a: A 500 kcal daily deficit loses about 0.45 kg per week. Larger deficits work faster but cost more muscle and are harder to sustain. Most people do best at 300-500 kcal.
faqs.q: What calorie deficit is best for weight loss?

faqs.a: Roughly 1 kg of body fat holds about 7,700 kcal, so a 500 kcal daily deficit predicts about 0.45 kg per week. Real loss varies with water shifts and muscle changes.
faqs.q: How fast will I lose weight?

faqs.a: Add 250-300 kcal above maintenance with progressive strength training. Faster surpluses mostly add fat, not muscle.
faqs.q: How should I eat to gain muscle?

faqs.a: Yes, but pick one: eat at maintenance while training hard (slow body recomposition) or alternate short gaining and cutting phases. Doing both at full speed is not realistic.
faqs.q: Can I lose fat and gain muscle at once?

faqs.a: BMR falls with weight, activity often drops unconsciously, and water retention masks fat loss. Recalculate TDEE, track honestly for two weeks, and only then adjust.
faqs.q: Why did my weight loss stall?

faqs.a: No. The formula is validated for adults. Children and teenagers need pediatric equations and a clinician's guidance.

tdee-calculator.formula:
TDEE = BMR x activity factor.
BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor, male) = 10 x kg + 6.25 x cm - 5 x age + 5.
Activity factors: 1.2 sedentary, 1.375 light, 1.55 moderate, 1.725 active, 1.9 very active.
Goal target = TDEE - 500 (lose), TDEE (maintain), TDEE + 500 (gain).
howTo: Select Male or Female and pick metric (cm/kg) or imperial (ft/in, lb).
Enter your age, height and weight.
Choose the activity level that best describes your typical week.
Pick your goal: lose, maintain or gain weight.
Read your TDEE, your daily calorie target and your expected weekly pace.
keyFacts: TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) is all the calories you burn in 24 hours.
It has four parts: BMR (60-70%), food digestion (about 10%), exercise and daily movement.
Activity factors multiply BMR: 1.2 for sedentary up to 1.9 for very active.
A 500 kcal daily deficit or surplus moves weight about 0.45 kg per week.
Weight change is driven by average intake over weeks, not single days.
A 30-year-old man at 70 kg, 175 cm, moderately active, burns about 2,556 kcal per day.

Cannot see muscle mass, so it underestimates muscular people.

An estimate for planning, not a medical prescription.

tdee-calculator.quickAnswer: TDEE is everything you burn in a day: BMR times an activity factor. A 30-year-old man at 70 kg and 175 cm, moderately active, has a TDEE of about 2,556 kcal/day. To lose weight at a steady 0.45 kg per week, the target is 2,056 kcal/day; to gain, 3,056 kcal/day.

tdee-calculator.workedExample:
Male, 30 years, 70 kg, 175 cm, moderate activity, goal: lose weight:
1. BMR = 10 x 70 + 6.25 x 175 - 5 x 30 + 5 = 1,649 kcal.
2. TDEE = 1,649 x 1.55 = 2,555.95, about 2,556 kcal/day.
3. Lose goal: 2,556 - 500 = 2,056 kcal/day.
4. Expected pace: 500 x 7 / 7,700 = 0.45 kg lost per week.
